text.content:
A heist runs in five phases: the briefing, the plan, the job, the scramble, and the debrief where everyone agrees it went fine and no one mentions the cat.

PhaseSummary
1 — The ScoreThe ST presents the job and the visible map — geography, obvious features, the objective, threats in plain sight. Roleplay only. No rolls, no Alert.
2 — PlanningCase for intel (each Success = one true detail the ST is holding; Casing reveals at most what the ST is holding — extra Successes buy nothing — and never the unknown obstacle). Make Preparations — one per spider; tactical setup, not auto-wins; each gets a complication that adds texture. Choosing entry squares is free, and so is anything a Perk grants (a Contingency, a Shortcut, a Trap, Planted Evidence, the Ghost's Dead Drop). A Silk Line pre-placed on a route you know costs no SP and, like any Silk Line, lowers that climb or crossing's Difficulty by 1; it doesn't skip it. A stashed item goes in a square you've cased.
3 — The Heist3–4 obstacles, each taking two successful rolls (Partial or better; a Critical counts as one) — one to get into position, one to do the job; a group check counts as both. The Alert starts at 0 and climbs. At least one obstacle is something the crew didn't uncover in Planning. Waiting isn't free: when the crew starts a third round at one obstacle, the ST rolls a Mid-Heist Complication.
4 — The Escape1–2 obstacles, one successful roll each. The Alert carries over unchanged. At least one obstacle must be solvable without Athletics — every spider needs a way to contribute.
5 — The DebriefCount the loot, award AP, argue about what went wrong, take the next job. They're always interested.

A scene is one obstacle — heist or Escape. Planning is its own scene, and silk placed during Planning lasts until the heist ends or it's broken.

A heist obstacle takes two successful rolls (Partial or better) — one to get into position, one to do the job — by the same spider or by different ones. When the whole crew must get past it together, a group check counts as both: the obstacle is done once every spider is through, and a spider who fails tries again next round. An Escape obstacle takes one successful roll — one spider's, or a group check with every spider through — and that roll covers the whole way through it: nobody rolls again for a squeeze or a climb along the route.

“Once per scene” and “once per heist” count for each player's spider separately; a Waiting Web replacement carries on with the uses its player has left. Damage Control and Not Part of the Plan belong to the whole crew: once per heist between them.

The crew is out and mostly alive. Count what they got. AP are per spider: every player earns the full amount below, for the original spider and any replacement alike. It isn't split. The one exception: a player whose spider was caught in the last Escape obstacle earns half, rounded down — the crew got out; they didn't.

OutcomeAdvancement Points
Full SuccessEscaped with the complete objective. Full AP for the difficulty: Easy 2, Standard 3, Hard 5, Absurd 6, Legendary 8.
Partial SuccessEscaped alive but without the objective, or with incomplete loot — part of it left behind or destroyed, which the ST says when it happens. Half AP, rounded down.
LossThe whole crew went Out before escaping. (Replacements arrive at the next obstacle, so a Loss means every spider is Out at the same time.) No AP. Significant embarrassment. Not discussed.

Spending AP

CostEffect
1 AP+1 to a Skill.
2 AP+1 to an Attribute.
3 APA new Perk from your Role list (no maximum).

After creation, Skills and Attributes can reach 5 (Attributes include the species bonus); the creation cap of 3 no longer applies. Unspent AP carry over. You start every heist Unharmed, with WIT + NERVE + 1 Silk Points, using your current WIT and NERVE (still without the species bonus).

Win: escape with the objective. Partial win: escape without it, everybody lives. Loss: the entire crew goes Out before anyone gets clear. Full Alert costs nothing extra here: getting out through it was the cost.

TierDescriptionCarrying It
Crumb (Easy)A single bit of food, a small charm, a coin. Simple job, modest reward.One spider, full Speed.
Trinket (Easy)A small shiny thing, a memory stick, a piece of jewelry light enough to move.One spider, full Speed.
Prize (Standard)Something significant — the main event of a proper heist. Full reward on success.One at half Speed, or two at full.
Treasure (Hard or Absurd)High value, high security, genuinely dangerous to take.Two at half Speed, or a silk sled (1 SP) at full.
The Big Score (Legendary)The kind of job spiders tell the spiderlings about. Maximum reward. Maximum everything-went-wrong.Everyone present, at half Speed, and a plan.

Carriers still act. Handing loot over is free; picking it up takes one Action by one spider, whatever its size — the other carriers just need to be adjacent to it. One spider can hold any loot in place, but it moves only with the carriers its row lists (a lone Treasure carrier stays put). Anything bigger than a Trinket won't fit a squeeze — find another way, or break off what fits and call it incomplete.
